entities.summary: Ludolph of Ratzeburg was a Premonstratensian Bishop of Ratzeburg, serving from 1223 to 1250. Born in the Holy Roman Empire, he was consecrated as bishop and played a significant role in the religious and administrative life of his diocese. Ludolph was a key figure in the ratification of the Concordat of Worms, a treaty between the Holy Roman Empire and the Catholic Church that aimed to strengthen the power of the papacy. He also participated in the Second Lateran Council, where he contributed to the formulation of the council's decrees. Ludolph's legacy can be seen in the continued development of the Premonstratensian Order, which he helped shape during his tenure. His contributions to the religious and administrative landscape of medieval Europe have had a lasting impact on the history of the Catholic Church and the Holy Roman Empire.
